THE END

But wait… it isn't the end! If you'd like (and can), you should post your gifts to the site! You don't need to post immediately, however; you should still seek critique on it if you haven't already. But, if you feel confident in your gift and have received applicable critique, post your gift (tale, SCP, etc.) the same way you'd post any article on the site. Once you've done so…

Add your gift here!

This is the Art Exchange hub. Go to the part where it says 2020 Holiday Art Exchange. Under it, you should see a link or two, or three, or ten, depending on when you get there. That is the list of posted Art Exchange articles. You can simply add your article to the bottom of the list! Also, tag your articles with the art-exchange tag. This helps categorization.

Note, only post gifts you made, not the ones your gifter made you.

But wait… something stirs in the wind… is there… yes, there is a new aspect to the Art Exchange this year! You can also post visual art and media to the Art Exchange Hub! This has been an aspect long missing from previous art exchanges, but underneath the list of articles is now a spot for the media arts of the Art Exchange. Expecting it will mostly be visual arts, there is currently a placeholder image and example text beneath it that the first artist to post can simply replace. From then on, further artists can copy and paste the module already there. Don't be too afraid of messing it up if you're as clumsy with code as I am; if something is less-than-pretty, Elogee or myself will fix it up later. Contact Elogee or myself if you have media that isn't visual that you'd like to add, and we'll figure out how best to add it!

Furthermore (this is quite an info-dump isn't it?), if you have a piece that you made for the Art Exchange that you don't think will stand up as a solo article but also don't think you either want to or can get critique enough to get to that point (an edge case I know but bear with me), you can add your article to the list of articles but under a collapsible instead of as a link! It's been done once in a previous Art Exchange, and I think that it could be very fun to have little mini-pieces that you can only read on the Art Exchange hub itself.

& So We Come to a Close

Thank you all so, so much for participating, I love putting this on every year, and it looks like it's going to be tradition that Elogee FishTruck and I will share this burden (not that it feels much like one). Thank you so much to Elogee FishTruck, who I at first put down as my "assistant" but who ended up doing at least as much as I did and so is truly and fully a cohost.

Huge thank you, also, to all the pinch-hitters who gave their time and offered their skills to come in clutch for people whose giftees couldn't make it for one reason or another.

I hope to see you all next year. Happy posting~!

item.title: THE GREAT REVIEW: ELECTRIC BOOGALOO
item.content:encoded:
Greetings! If you don't know who I am, I'm Jak. As DarkStuff alluded to in their post, they may be a bit busy with other things. So, in order to help them and to also make sure that everyone has their gifts reviewed before the 29th, I have offered to step in and help with the remaining articles. But hey, if you were looking forward to DarkStuff's review then no worries! They have said that they will get to everyones eventually. Even if it meant going beyond the 29th to read/review them all. So, with that being said: let the reviews continue! (Please note that I also will more-than-likely lack the proper context for most of these articles. So, consider this a fresh pair of eyes!)

aismallard's Gift
Pukae

This is a Tale involving RAISA, and as aismallard aptly put it: "an interesting tale that shows the atmosphere and stress of working at both a rigorous technical position and the weird anomalous environments Foundation employees find themselves in." The prose in this article is astonishingly good. I found myself invested in Flynn's engagement on Site-64 throughout the article. With the water-cooler talk, to the emails, to the ghost chicken. Everything was so smooth. Including Flynn themself, who felt like they were actually suffering from a late, overtime shift. The narrative was so fun, and that ending made me chuckle out loud. This was honestly a nice take on RAISA, and something I want to see more of post-exchange. Seriously, I loved this piece. My only problem (which was self-induced), was that I did have a bit of trouble staying on track with what the "Crocodile" is, but I'll chop that up to my fault over the author, since they did an amazing job walking the reader along. Great work!

Alces_alces's Gift
craydaddy's SoundCloud Page

This is a new image for SCP-3604 depicting user "craydaddy's" SoundCloud page. And honestly, it's such a cute idea! I thought for a second that it was just a photo-edited SoundCloud picture but no, it legitimately exists. I won't get too into it, since I don't believe it's necessarily the focus of this piece but I figured I'd add it. But no, going into the image itself? I love craydaddy's Top Tracks (specifically "THIS BITCH CRAY CRAY"). Their bio is also hilarious, really giving off that "SoundCloud rapper" vibe, which I think is the point? The likes to other crayfish-related content is also a nice touch. All-in-all, a super inventive gift. I personally adore it!

AnAnomalousWriter's Gift
Wallpapers!

This, this, this, and this are beautiful SCP-related wallpapers/images! First, before I get into the specifics of each one: I really love the simplicity behind all of these. They're bold, impactful, and quite honestly most of these are super easy on the eyes (which, if you're going to use these as wallpapers, is a good idea. Messy art with lines going everywhere and whatnot can be really hard to see!) But, let me get into each one:

This, is probably my favorite. From the background, it almost looks like this took some inspiration of the BHL Overwatch Command theme? Regardless, I love it. I really like how the Foundation symbol in the back is a different color than the text in front of it. It really makes a difference between the "Secure, Contain, Protect" with everything else (TL;DR less mess and less strain to see the text). Fantastic work!

This appears to be the same image as the previous, but with an interesting blood splatter mixed with it. Admittedly, I personally prefer the one without it, but I think it does add a bit of contrast nonetheless. Nothing really else to add, besides the blood splatter looks really, really well done!

This has some definite potential. The bold insignia on the right side looks insanely good. I even like the blue hues, even if I prefer them to be slightly darker. My only big problem with this is the text itself. The white text in front of the super-light background makes it hard to read (especially for someone with a light astigmatism!) I think if the text was perhaps a darker color, or the background was darker it would look even more amazing!

This is a neat little insignia for the SCP logo. I'm a bit puzzled as to what this was intended to be, or if it contains any significant meaning beyond just being a cool image, but I absolutely dig it! I wish I had more to say with this one: but I just don't have enough context. It looks good! :)

BlueJones's Gift
An Exciting Tale of Two Groups!

This is a particularly interesting Tale surrounding the Shark Punching Center and… another group? Honestly, I wanted to love this so bad. I really enjoy Tales surrounding space exploration and weird/odd extraterrestrial objects and structures, so it lined up really well in that regard. Heck, by the end of the reading, I was actually surprised and interesting in the concept of the Moon once being human (it really reminded me of Rise of the Guardians, if anyone knows that Disney movie). However… the prose is really shaky and rough. There were a lot of SPaG mistakes that sort of took me out of my immersion, as well as some really oddly formatted and structured sentences/paragraphs that really made me feel lost. At one point, it tried to detail a pretty interesting timeline: but really it just felt like an exposition dump instead of something that benefited the overall theme. However, I think that with a bit of reworking, corrections, and a helpful hand: this Tale could really do something well! Great job!

Crashington's Gift
Getting Over It

This is lovely fan-art depicting the subject in SCP-4376. Since I have never read SCP-4376, I will only be able to talk about the art itself. And wow. First, I adore the shading, texture, and colors used in this piece. I have always enjoyed some grain or grit when it comes to art, and for me personally, this compliments my tastes well (even though it's not tailored to me at all). The linework is clean and crisp, with the overall style reminding me of a more cartoon-y, Total Drama Island aesthetic (which I love). The facial features, pose, even how the hands and details in the clothes are drawn are so nice and lovely. This piece gets my seal of approval. Keep doing fantastic art!

Connor MacWarren's Gift
A Working Theory

This is a tale relating to MacWarren's author avatar, Dr. Connor MacWarren. The tale itself was somewhat difficult for me to follow through parts but definitely a worthwhile read. I really enjoyed the characterization of Dr. MacWarren and his interactions with the other personnel, and the climax with the tunnel generator failing was really fun. I also liked Dr. Pheonix's interjections throughout, even if they did feel somewhat confusing and misplaced at first. The ending concluded at a rather decent hook, leaving me wondering exactly what the file that the Memetics Department was keeping away from Dr. Henshaw was really all about. I'd argue that this was missing some further fleshing out, but that shouldn't detract from what's there now (and it's definitely interesting). Despite that, and some minor tone/SPaG errors, I had a lot of fun with this!

Deadly Bread's Gift
Where the Smoke Trail Ends

This is an SCP document relating to Fifthism, memes, cross-anomalous contamination, and SCP-5993. Although I hate to admit it, I am definitely missing some context with this article. Being still new to the concept of Fifthism, and not having read SCP-5993, it was hard for me to really follow at points. That being said, this is some high quality work. The clinical tone is really nice, and the incorporation of the multiple Departments and crosslinks related to Fifthism was fun. I really enjoyed the ending, after finally figuring out what had happened to allow an anomaly like this to occur. The addenda really stack onto another nicely and coherently. I loved the Experiment/Unusual incidents as well since they really brought out this concept well. And that picture. Great usage of media to help really tie together the ending. Bravo!

Ethagon's Gift
Explanation and Research Department

This is a very creative gift: A Site-Dossier for a "Explanation and Research Department" (EXaRD). Frankly, the only upsetting part of this article is the amount of information that simply couldn't be shared—whether that be from things still not being determined yet, or simply having no extra content that helps tie it together. HOWEVER. What is there is nothing short of impressing. I am incredibly excited to see this get updated and posted. I love the in-depth Site Overview with the separate Research, Reclassification, and Release initiatives being amazingly intriguing. Honestly the entire prospect of this Department and its interactions with -EX anomalys is super sweet, and this Dossier compliments that by a large, large margin. It's clear, concise, and I can tell that a lot of detail definitely went into it in order to make it seem real. Can't wait to see this fleshed out and expanded upon by each of you!

General Goose's Gift
To Simply Be Loved

This is a cutesy tale surrounding SCP-4576, a toy cactus. Right off the bat, the usage of media is really pleasing. The fact that this appears to be art made specifically for this piece makes it all the more wonderful. The beginning leads strong, with the article detailing the distraught and sadness of forgotten toys. I won't spoil the ending since it's very cute, but I liked what this tale was going for. It does feel kind of rushed, with multiple SPaG errors (including missing words and some incorrect phrases). I should also mention that without reading SCP-4576 (which I really need to now!), it was hard to follow along, especially when it off-handedly introduce characters that the reader has never actually met. But regardless of that, it was otherwise super imaginative! The prose really felt tied to the perspective. Solid work from this gift!

JackalRelated's Gift
Operation Report #A271

This is a very engaging Tale involving Dr. Clef, SCP-4917 (which, unfortunately, I haven't actually read), and getting arrested within a lucid dream. And just… this was so perfect. The wacky, dream-like atmosphere was retained via the character descriptions, engagement, and the series-of-events that were described throughout the trial. I really don't want to spoil that ending since it's very humorous, but this Tale seriously kept a smile on my face throughout. The page was also wonderfully formatted, and the character's dialogue (which this really relied on) was so solid that it's frankly astonishing. I kind of wish that Clef was a bit more fleshed out, but considering the context of the Tale and what was happening, it makes sense that he was put on the backburner. Regardless, utterly fun article. I cannot wait to upvote this and go into even more detail with my review once everyone learns of the gifters identity. Great work!

Lazar Lyusternik's Gift
Setting Sun

This is a breathtaking piece of O5-10, which also hints to his source tale, Setting Sun. And… wow. As I alluded to in another review, I love dark, grimey, and gritty undertones and this piece delivers just that. From the sketchy-thin lines to the shadows casted along O5-10's shoulders: I am immensely impressed. I love the redaction along his face, and the sinister-looking portrait he is displaying to the viewer that depicts a shadow-y figure with glowing eyes. And don't even get me started on the background. The red-toned sun? The blur-effect surrounding O5-10 and the redaction? They're all executed so well that it's shocking. This would be something I put on my lock-screen because frankly, it's outstanding. Will definitely be reading the Setting Sun tale after seeing this beautiful artwork. Congrats artist!

LordStonefish's Gift
Here be Gifts!

This is a very interesting tale surrounding the Glittering Horizons Series. Admittedly, I really lack the context surrounding the series of events with Van Turner, the Department of Photography, and everything else. Regardless, this was an extremely fun little piece. I personally enjoyed the duality between Van Turner's proposal towards the Council and Joseph being chased down by his mysterious gunman. The action between the two was definitely there and really kept me engaged throughout. The progression between the two also really flowed well for me, and the ending definitely left me wondering. Why did they do this? What's the bigger play at hand here? What's the real reason behind this all? A wonderful piece narratively, with smooth prose and detailed imagery to really nail things together. Great job author!

Lt Flops's Gift
Team Bird!!!

This Is lovely art for the Team Bird Series! I must say: this art is super beautiful. From the linework to the little details of the background, it all works together really well. The colors are really nice, with the added texture really tying it all together. I am very interested to see what the hieroglyphics mean behind the pigeons and on the side of the piece itself. Thoth himself looks super nice, with the pose really matching that of other ancient Egyptian pieces (or so I've seen). All-in-all, this is a very cute piece of art. Like I said, I adore the detail and the overall style and feel of it as a whole. Fantastic work!

MalyceGraves's Gift
Lovely, Melancholy Art

This is fanart for SCP-4459 and it's stunningly beautiful. The structure of the piece itself really moves your eyes towards the center, leading you to (what I'm assuming) is the anomaly itself. Taking a step back, however, and you can begin to see that this image has so much interesting detail. First, I love the grey-toned grass and smoke in the setting. It gives off a very mystique mood that vibes heavily within me. The liquid dripping from the hat, onto the floor looks like if outer space had literally melted (which is just SO cool, but I have no idea if that was intentional). In the background, the silhouettes of the tents and their flags really ties this entire thing together. I could go on, into the details of the closet (???) and the object below the hat itself, but I think my point has been made. Fantastic art, completely!

OriCat's Gift
Crazy SCP Fuel!

This, this, this, and this are amazingly realistic photos of potential SCP's! And… wow. The quality is absolutely stunning. These all look like they could exist, and they're so mind-bogglingly interesting and compelling. I am thoroughly excited to see any/all of these in a future article because they look just so amazing. Here, let's go in-depth:

This looks absolutely crazy. As OriCat said in their post, "'photo-manips of deformed organisms I could use for articles'" and this nails it. The perspective and effects of the photo are interesting. When I first saw it, I assumed that this could be used for like, an aquatic or perhaps extraterrestrial anomaly. The creature itself is amazingly well-done. I am thoroughly impressed by how this organism looks in the context of the entire picture itself. I have no words beyond utter fascination. Probably my favorite one!

This looks insanely freaky. I don't really know why this organism is just lying around on a wooden patio (again, potential fuel) but I'm not going to complain. The amount of tentacles it has is strangely concerning, and that eye is super, super weird. I will say though: the eye does look a bit added in. However, that doesn't really detract much from the image itself. Super creepy!

This is the same as the previous, but with a super neat filter/effect instead of a static image. Although I personally find it somewhat appealing: I could definitely see this being a bit of problem for other viewers. The added noise makes it hard to really focus on what's important, and the issue with the creature's eye feels even more apparent with this image. Still, though, I can't get over how impressive it looks!

This is an insanely neat picture of a human skeleton. You could definitely do something with this: particular surrounding an archaeological site or something similar. The weird engravings/wounds/things along the front and sides of the skull itself are really nice. This image is probably the one I'm most looking forward to in an article, since it seems like the most "tame" picture of the other three. Absolutely beautiful work gifter!

Raptie's Gift
KTO-0001-Bellfather

This is an astonishing GOC article that flips the Foundation on-top of its head. First, the content warning: please heed it. Okay, going into the article itself: I'm blown away. This concept, just on its face, has so much potential. I love the idea behind the Foundation just being a rag-tag conglomeration of all the GoI's unilaterally hating the Coalition. "Keep your enemies closer," and all of that. I love the detail and synopsis of each of the Bellfather members. You can tell that a ton of time has been reserved for figuring out how to implement the differing characters and their involvement with the Foundation's directive. The format that it follows with the messages really helps the reader follow along with the article, with the ending being just so captivating. Seriously people, expand upon this. Characterizing the Overwatch Command like this could really lead to so much more good content. It also kinda revitalizes the "Foundation is evil" vibe that I've always digged. Good, good job author!

RhettyBoy's Gift
Space Odyssey/SCP-3001

This is a phenomenal depiction of SCP-3001, with the added aesthetic of being a movie poster which is awfully reminiscent of another popular film. And just… I'm blown away. I love the red-tinted (haha, duh "red" and all of that) control panel in the center. Your eyes get instantly attracted to it, really giving it atmosphere and an utter awe factor as well. The linework, the text, the shading, and the vignette? I frankly can't tell if this was all digitally drawn or if there was image manipulation happening but it's jaw-dropping. I very much enjoy the added information at the bottom, with the "cast" and the author of SCP-3001 being displayed. Quite frankly, I could see this being a legit movie poster, something I'd see walking into AMC or anywhere else. Great idea to provide a clean and withered version of it too! I think the withered version definitely gives it more oomph. Astonishing work, mysterious gifter!

ROUNDERHOUSE's Gift
Wonder

This is a beautiful article concerning the insight of the narrator's "wonder" with man—taking place within the universe of the Wanderer's Library. Firstly, I am thoroughly blown away by the prose. All of the sentences flow really well together, each having a powerful impact onto another as the story progresses. The structure, tone, and diction of the paragraphs really amplifies the narrator, all while providing a vivid depiction of how this entity perceives man. It dives into our goods and bads, our highs and lows, and our grandest achievements over the minor successes. This piece definitely inspires awe and wonder, giving the reader a chance to see ourselves through a different metaphorical lens. It's absolutely beautiful. I really hope this get's posted on the Wanderers Library because wow. An impressive piece!

stormbreath's Gift
SCP-5682 Art!

This (link appears blacklisted, check here for post!) is jaw-dropping fanart of SCP-5682. Conveniently, this is an article that I have actually read. And trust me when I say that when I first saw this fanart, I was shocked by how similar it was to picture in my head when I first read the article. But, moving along from that: I think this is outstanding. The surrealistic elements surrounding the perimeter of the building is so good. The grey-tones mixing with the white background actually makes this look super clean and vivid (along with the linework, of course). It almost reminds me of street-art with how they (the different parts of the background itself) almost flow outward. I really like the detail of the flames, the beam, and the building itself in the image. This does a really good job with contrasting aspects of the artwork in order to draw your eyes inward and towards the beam itself plus other areas of the piece. It's an absolute pleasure to see this, and I'm immensely surprised by how well-done it really is.

TheBlueHour's Gift
Wondertainment and Scarlet King

This is an absolutely astonishing hand-drawn depiction of Dr. Wondertainment Goes Out With a Bang. First, I absolutely love the Dr. Suess-esque inspiration with the setting. It matches my headcanon of Wondertainment well. The wavey, bright pastel-colors along with the bold, thick lines really layers this piece. The buildings themselves remind me of old "funhouses" at circuses or fairs that really makes it stand out. Not only that, but I adore the contrast between it and the Scarlet King with the flames. The chaos appears very well warranted, with the added details of the smoke giving the scene a very grand and impactful mood. That, with the visualization of the two characters, face-to-face? A very masterfully-crafted piece of artwork. And, as I said, the fact that it appears to be hand-drawn is even more astonishing!

This concludes the reviews! I hope everyone had as much fun with this as I did, including reviewing some of your works! I'm very excited to put faces and names behind all of these articles. Some shockingly fun stuff, so make sure you take a look for yourself before everyone gets revealed! You may end up being surprised. I know I sure will :)

item.title: THE GREAT REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
Last year, I read (slash viewed [slash experienced]) every art exchange gift and reviewed them. I think I would like to do that once again. This forum post will be edited over the coming days to start cataloguing and commenting on every single art exchange piece. That's right!

For convenience, this will be organized by the alphabetical order of the recipient. So, when this post gets edited, the new additions may not necessarily be at the bottom. Also, I am writing this at a rather busy time, so it will take a bit for this to really start filling up. But, anyhow… here we go!

Aethris' gift
AFTER ACTION REPORT

This is an MTF raid of a sarkic compound with an unusually festive twist right at the end (though in hindsight it was indeed hinted at). There are some pretty big breaches in what should be clinical tone, and not in the dialogue (where such things are accepted), and one instance of some messed up formatting, but besides these minor complaints, the tale is very fun. I like the background before the MTF (Tau-5, "Samsara) goes in to clear things out. I like the descriptions of the weapons they are armed with. I think the twist could have been a bit more hinted at — as is, when people read this story in the future, I think it will come out of complete left field — but if foreshadowed better could be exceptionally funny and creative. Pacing good, Samsara good (kind of creepy in how robotic they talked), lore good, tale good.

AgentAX's gift
Melody for a Tortured Soul

This is a story whose emotional impact was aided by my having Spirited Away's end credits song playing in the background while I read… but nonetheless, it's about a guy learning a better way to cope. Pretty short, didn't hit as hard as it could have (I had not much reason to get attached to this character), and a bit on the nose at the end, but not bad in any respects. Good incorporation of SCP-4562, as well.

Attila the Pun's gift
Jalesveva

This is a tale I have trouble following. I'm missing the context on who Raven's Gate is, and I just generally have trouble figure out what's going on. I think someone pulled a heist on a ship that they thought had info on it, but instead had a nuke, and they also got caught(?) and trapped on the ship by the GOC (who owned the ship), and then the ship set sail, they thought of an escape plan, executed it, and left. That's my best guess. I'm glad it made Attila happy, I wish I could parse it better, at the very least I can tell it appealed directly to the giftee's sensibilities and the ideas are inarguably fun.

Calibri Bold's gift
It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Eldritch

This is a sung rendition of a parody of It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas that Calibri wrote. I have no fucking clue who this bearded individual could possibly be. It's a huge mystery to me. But whoever they are, they have a pretty solid voice, and this made me smile. I bet it made Calibri smile at least twice as much, seeing as it was their own parody. Very festive gift.

Captain Kirby's gift
CactusCast

This is a very funny story about SCP-3388. Poky wreaks havoc across the internet. It is very funny, and made me smile, and made me chuckle. Good tale. Excited to see this posted. Oh, of note is that Kirby got another gift, but I already reviewed it as one of Tufto's gifts, as it seems to have been a gift to both of them.

Dysadron's gift
The Definition of Madness

This is… damn. This is really good. I didn't need the context of the associated SCP to get what was going on. It's simple, it's creepy, it's believable, the black bars are a great touch, ending was damn good. Just enough background on the character to make me connect to them as another human being. Definitely expected the movie to be anomalous, didn't expect it to be anomalous in that way. I expected something more… murdery happening to the person who watched it. I guess this is more a compliment on the SCP it's based off of — SCP-5733 — but great anomaly. Just all around great. Damn.

Dr Whitney's gift
Where Do You Belong?

This is a tale that, for being comedic at its core, has a pretty great grasp on theming. We follow a character, Dr. Whitney (I wonder why?), who is a big lizard woman and interviews a bunch of people who try to steal some frog bones. Each of the interviews conducted has an underlying theme of not being accepted for who you are, with various spins. I definitely think that, to make the build stronger, the clockwork woman should have come last, as that was the least comical interview and the strongest holder of the theme, but after that we just get a brief moment of recollection for Dr. Whitney as she sees some "normal" people having a normal get-together and being jealous for a brief moment. For being as silly as it is, major props to the progression and idea of this article. I critiqued it, and I'm glad to see how far it has come. I know the author was originally unhappy with the ending, and I never got around to critiquing the newest version to help with that, but honestly, I like the ending as it is. Good shit.

Ellie3's gift
The Serpent Searches About

This is art of Ellie3's canon resurrection team's version of the Serpent in the War on All Fronts canon. I admittedly have read very little of it except for one WWS piece that they wrote (Cappi), but this depiction of the Serpent makes me want to read more. I was just about to say "based on the art style I'm pretty certain I know who made it", but I hosted this whole thing, of course I know who it is! No being cheeky for me, then, heheh. Anyhow, very amazingly cool. Also, I see you, Rounderpede.

Gabriel McQueen's gift
Stranded Heartstrings

This is a delightfully disturbing real-feeling story. I want to say very little about it so as not to spoil it. I do think that in the climax, the laughing felt out of place and out of character. There was also a description of something becoming louder despite the fact it's established the cameras don't have sound detection. But, yeah. Captivating. Disturbing. I will have more to say when this is posted — and it had better be posted, because damn. Oh, and while I don't think the SCP Foundation would ever have content warnings, I support the execution the author used here, keeping the content warning in-universe. Despite it feeling out-of-character for the Foundation, it aids in immersion, so if you must have a content warning in an SCP article, I do recommend this method.

Alright fine I decided I have more to say. This almost felt like one of those skips that was a glorified tale, where the anomaly isn't really necessary for the story and in fact is just a framework so that the author can write their tale idea in clinical tone and on the mainlist where it will get more attention. However, the ending pulled it back around, and I really appreciate that. Okay, now I'm done.

Gaffsey's gift
Heresiographer

This is a fantastic article about a semi-Fifthist artifact's interactions with a Viatnamese uprising against French rule in the late 1930s. It's pretty amazing how much detail the author went into, and it's extra amazing how much character he wrote in. You can feel the love for history here. It's not just an interesting conflict in its own right, but it talks about how information gets recorded in the first place, carrying a theme of "your version of the truth", between how the Japanese interacted with the rock, the American talked about his view of the Vietnamese, and how the Vietnamese viewed the struggle, all with the central thematic piece of the pink rock which is "raw power", shaped by the wants and views of those who used it. It is an intimidatingly coherent piece with clear Lovecraftian inspiration (I know, I know, you can use "cosmic horror" to avoid attributing everything to direct Lovecraft inspiration nowadays but this is even set in the 1930s, you gotta realize that that's really contributing to the Lovecraft vibe here) as I always love to see in these Fifthist pieces. Good fucking job. One of the most solid creations for this art exchange.

Henzoid's gift
New York Times Op-Ed

This is a fun little piece set in the Broken Masquerade canon, inspired by Henzoid's own Demasqed series. I haven't read it, but the themes are obvious. It feels like you can easily jump into this tale with no background. The commentary is great, I'm always one for exposing the inherent evil of companies and the twisted conservatism of maintaining status quos purely for the sake of it, so… yeah I like this, heehee.

Its a Bad Idea
The Sunset

This is a song, just a piano song. I don't know what request of Its a Bad Idea's this fulfills — as in, I don't know if this connects to anything they wrote or not. I'm sure Bad Idea knows. In any case, it's a beautiful, snowy piano piece. Sleepy. Peaceful. The piano player pauses sometimes, in a way that suggests to me that they aren't practiced enough to keep it up with no mistakes. I point this out because that adds to the homely feeling of it all (I use "homely" with my own definition, it's so weird that word technically means "ugly"). Very good. Nice art to use as the thumbnail as well, no clue if that's original or not.

J Dune's gift
Oh No, Burger!

This is a rather funny artpiece in reference to SCP-5818, which I haven't read. I only know that they fear… the burger. The faces are cartoony and fun. Just a goofy little image. I like it.

Jacob Conwell's gift
Dire Wolf

This is a very long tale about Conwell's character, Phineas, who co-founded Anderson Robotics, a GoI I haven't really explored until just recently. I find the main character intriguing, and I find the pacing mostly on point. If I had a major complaint, I'd say the ending is rather anticlimactic. The tale itself points this out, but I'm not sure if I like it even still. But, it seems Conwell enjoyed it, and the sheer wordcount here is high above the usual for an Art Exchange tale, so he got a rather big gift!

JakdragonX's gift
Life Like a Box of Chocolates

This is art of SCP-5346, which I admittedly have never read. Nonetheless, it looks like it was painted on actual canvas (that or they have a digital art filter that does that, either way it looks cool) and the eye, the hands, and the… whatever is covering where "is" should be in this saying… it looks hella neat! Wonderful gift.

Jakob17's gifts
The Old Man's Comeback

This is a tale that is unfortunately unfinished, but has a promising start. It looks like it's going to go into a bit of backstory for SCP-106, but not like The Young Man covers. History of how the Foundation got it. Prose is solid, hope to see it finished eventually. For now, it's a good teaser. Good thing it was paired with…

This tale, of SCP-106 emerging from a broken Foundation site to walk through a ravaged, empty world. I think there are some pretty neat themes here, even if it is a rather short little thing. I like the use of the lore from the Young Man, and I like the use of the song lyrics from the Irish folk song. Good, simple stuff.

Karablue9482's gift
Bird Eats

This was an absolute rollercoaster. Firstly, I'd never seen this CSS before. I quickly discovered that the author had not invented it themselves, but nonetheless it is stunning and impressed me immediately. Then, I read the actual content, and it's a food critic reviewing an artiste's recipe that they made. Oh, and the characters are birds. The actual content of the article is exceptionally captivating, like, I have never ever cared this much about food. There are some inconsistencies with the neopronouns (as far as I know, maybe "her" and "hir" are meant to be interchangeable?) and generally just some minor errors, but not nearly enough to notably change my enjoyment of the article. The characters are strange and interesting. The pacing is fantastic. The content is elegantly simple, and equally elegantly executed. And furthermore, I looked it up, and this is the author's first thing written for SCP. They otherwise don't exist as an author, as far as I can tell. That is. Actually unbelievable.

I pray to a God I don't believe in that this person A] posts this to the site and B] starts writing a lot more afterwards.

kinchtheknifeblade's gift
Gamers Against Quarantine

This is a Very COVID Christmas™️, with some people having anxiety that gets relieved by taking a step outside, something which some of us are unfortunate enough not to be able to do. I'm grateful for living in a small town on a private road, where I can walk my dog and not worry about coming into contact with people for the most part, but (sorry to get a little real here in the Art Exchange) I feel really bad for people living in apartment complexes. I hope you're holding up, wherever you are.

In any case, this tale does the feeling of pandemic anxiety justice. Good characterization, good feels (mostly). Bittersweet and I like it.

KirQ's gift
Hanukkah Spirit

This is an injection of holiday spirit outside Christmas for this art exchange, a wonderful Hanukkah tale. I think you can tell it's a bit rushed, with how many spelling errors and formatting whoopsies it has, but I feel okay pointing that out because it dovetails into a compliment; assuming this is a pinch-hitter, they did really well with limited time. The character interactions were very funny, the situation was humorous, the observations were witty, Atlas and Ibis (though I don't know if they were original characters) were interesting and fun, and I just liked it overall. Festive ae-eff. Keep it up.

Luxkeeper's gift
A Beautiful Palace

Holy shit, more pixel art in this art exchange? This is a palace in the clouds (SCP-4840) above a picturesque lake and forest, done in pixel art fashion! Makes me think whoever did the diner pixel art must've been a pinch-hitter, and like… wow, that means one of these two pieces was probably made in 48 hours. Which is amazing. Either way, this is crazy awesome. Serene is a word for it. Impressive is another. Great work.

MaliceAforethought's gifts
A Whole Bunch of Stuff

This is a collection of things. Three photoshopped images, what looks like a pen or pencil drawing, and then a tale, all by the same person!? This is really fantastic. The tale has some prose stuff I'd love to see tightened (like their handling of quotes within quotes and some odd punctuations with commas), but besides that it is a well-paced, highly intriguing view of two organizations doing dealings with one another against The Foundation. The UIU, and MI13 (or Her Majesty's Foundation for Secure Containment of the Paranormal). It's a lore dump that I am extremely into. Its explanation of the Romans versus the Celts and Picts leaving behind anomalous phenomena was quick and wonderful, as was its pointing out that the British Museum was rife with anomalous artifacts. This world it painted, the world of the anomalous scene in London, was complete, intriguing, and fit for a paranormal spy setting. Absolutely amazing. Oh, and the images were pretty great too, but my love lies with the writing.

Malvarik1's gifts
Author Avatar & Pixel Art

This is… maybe an author avatar, created for Malvarik? Malvarik themselves said they didn't know what exactly it was fulfilling, but nonetheless, SCP researcher art has been received and appreciated.

This is some pixel art of a diner that Malvarik made. It's pretty wonderful, reminds me of the diner in a train car from the game Night in the Woods, and I think I see The Beast from Over the Garden Wall? Not that shadowy figures with antlers only exist in that show, but I am heavily reminded of him. May have been intentional, may not have been. In any case, very skillful work, I wanna play a game in this artstyle.

margssentif's gift
Kakapo Baby

This is a clay figure of marg's WWS critter, Arorangi! I actually have a bit of a story for this one. I did this for multiple people, but, when people offered their specific artistic talents, I was looking for people requesting artpieces who I thought had articles to make art of that really meshed with the artist's style. I was trying to make sure that the person who made this art (rather obvious to people like me but some people may be none-the-wiser) would have something they could easily take inspiration from. When I gave marg to them, the thought was "I would love to see Arorangi in this person's style". That was the reason I gave them to marg. And it worked out. I am an evil Christmas mastermind, mwahahaha!

(It's very good I like it a lot.)

Modulum's gift
Black Hole City

This is unbelievably incredible. This looks like art you would have to pay to get. Like, this looks like art created by someone who's already made it in their artistic career. It's exactly as Modulum describes it — "dark, grand, cinematic, and apocalyptic". The colors are great, the details are great, the landscape is great, the atmosphere is great, it's great, it's all great. Fuck, it's great.

Nagiros' gift
Trapped in a Site

This is the type of story where I am certain the person who received it would smile from ear to ear reading it. I don't know who "Skippy" is, but Nagiros does, and their portrayal is simple, comical, and charming. The situation and dialogue in general is funny and well-written. The alarm clock is a great gag. Not much more to say. Good stuff!

not_a_seagull's gift
Audio Log

This is a really skillfully crafted audio log created for one of Seagull's articles, SCP-3248. I am of course missing context, but the audio mixing here is great! I wish the "time has passed" sound was less glitchy and more like that static you get from fast forwarding old cassettes (if I'm even remembering that noise correctly), because as it is it was pretty intrusive, but it communicated what it needed to effectively. This person must have had a good mic. Outside the box, too!

EDIT: It is, for some reason, not letting me add Seagull's link to his gift here. Uhh, so, instead, here is the link to his post, which in turn links to his gift: link.

Maybe not, I haven't read much of it.) However, it's fun for what it is. The woman is believable, I like Hopper as a dude, I like the premise, I only think that it's lacking in the action department. Placeholder MCD's gift
So Clean Mr. Measure

This is some mind-bendy Department of Miscommunications shit (yay, another baby of mine that has a life of its own on this site, love seeing these things crop up — though before you think me rude let me be the first to admit that it may be my baby but I am not the only parent) about music! I critiqued this before it got sent out, and I am glad to see the changes that happened. My favorite lines are still in here (Mr. Measure, a nice middle note) but a lot of what I felt was the more generic "going crazy" stuff is gone. I really have no idea what is happening in this skip (even though I know the Misters are the three computers), but I do really like it. Fits the DoMc vibe perfectly.

Ralliston's gift
Bear Flag Republic

This is a tale I am definitely missing context for, but the format and presentation is great. Forgive me, history was my worst subject in high school, but this sounds like the Spanish-American war, in which America pushed westward to take the Western Front "back" (huge emphasis on the quotation marks here) from the Spanish settlers. I love the aesthetic of the announcements and the letters, I don't fully understand what happened (Fremont met with a force, but then the force ceased to exist soon after, and yet the force was still hailed by the Spanish settlers, and apparently he was a bear?), but I enjoyed the ride thoroughly. Good stuff.

Retrom's gift
Observer

This is a tale that justifies its length. Usually, my sensibilities want these flash fiction things to be longer. (I am a bit against the grain of the site at large in that regard.) But this? This requires no extra context, no extra exploration, it amps up at a good clip, the prose is creepy as fuck… I like it a lot. This gifter achieved a lot with very little. Good job, good squick value.

Rigen's gift
Cooties!!

This is a skip about cooties. It's… actually really, really clever. I don't think I want to spoil it. It's strangely cute, rather funny, and wildly clever. Please read it. Great gift. Oh, and I just saw the URL, and what a pun, wow.

Sirslash47's gift
The Mannequin Troupe

This is a neat little poem in a format that I recognize but can't say the name of as I am not a poetry buff. The meter seemed a bit shaky, but perhaps I am simply not the best poem-reader, I often find it difficult to get into the groove of reading something to a rhythm if the number of syllables change. Makes me feel like I'm missing something. Anyhow, I feel I'm missing something here, but that is no matter. I like the format, I like the content, it's a fun little jaunt.

Skorpt's gift
Aztec God of War

This was an SCP written about the Aztec and Mayan mythology of Latin America, featuring a god of war, Huitzilopochtli. Its tone was pretty great. My only complaint is that Huitzilopochtli seems to spill their hand very all-of-a-sudden right at the end. Bit of an info-dump. Other than that, very solid.

stephlynch's gift
Oh My God, My Sides

This is absolutely amazing. The amount of effort put in here (creating a dance, the costume, the lighting) is phenomenal. The fact that they did something so wildly different from anything else in this art exchange is pretty radical. It's very obvious who made this gift if you scour the forum posts, but I honestly don't remember what their name was, so it's safe from me if I don't go peek at my magical behind-the-scenes spreadsheet. Very good. Very, very good. Made me smile from ear to ear. Everyone should watch this.

taylor_itkin's gift
You Can't Contain Us

These two versions of the same image depict Taylor's article SCP-3524. I like the colors, I like that there's a grimier version, I like the pose of the girl, I like it all. Good stuff.

The Pighead's gift
White Elephants for Black Queens

This is a festive Black Queen tale about a white elephant gift exchange. I'm not personally a fan of Black Queen, but from what I can tell this is faithful to the established Black Queen GoI format, and Pighead liked it, so it does what it sets out to accomplish! Something about putting aside differences for the holidays. Cute.

Tufto's gifts
Survivor & Code

This is a tale about a man surviving his house being burnt down (there is an implication of arson), not knowing whether his relatives he lived with are still alive, having no way to contact them if they are, and thus having to find a new way of life. The prose here makes me fucking jealous. It is tight as hell, atmospheric as all get-out, and makes this character from a very different culture from my own so very relatable in a way I could not have expected. I'm missing some context (SCP-4841) but I do not feel I need it. There are some absolutely stellar lines in here, and the ending is particularly… melancholy. Loved this, loved this so much.

This is a sermon given through the lens of code that relates to something Tufto and Kirby wrote together at some point. Knowing absolute dogshit about code, I think I missed a lot here, but the tone was interesting, I liked what I could tell of what was happening. 10/10 for aesthetics as well.

TyGently's gift
Laika Lives

This is a beautiful dog story. It's hard to go wrong with dog stories. Their simple minds and big hearts make them endearing protagonists immediately. I've already read the skip this is based on, and a graphic novel centered around Laika, so I'm already very invested in this adorable, tragic little dog. This delivers on that investment. A dog contemplating its own death is… not fun. And very well executed. Bravo.

Tyumen's gift
AIAD Magic

This is a great piece of art about some AIAD characters of Tyumen's, with some really striking colors mixed with a gray character. I love the contrast between the two. I like the character design, I like the pose, I like the background. All very, very good. Keep it up, artists!

UncertaintyCrossing's gift
The Vacancy

This is a story about the Library, featuring UncertainyCrossing's author avatar, Uncy, a masked dog that stalks the Archives of the Library. It's well written, pretty neat. I like it, but don't have much special to say about it. Simple solid tale.

Uncle Nicolini's gifts
The Fantastic Fae

This is a cute little well-wishes thing. It looks like we get meta here, and Fae is supposedly thanking her author (Nico) and wishing them a happy New Year and Merry Christmas. It's cute, if very short!

This is another very short story, this time about an interaction between Faeowynn and Dr. Everwood, Nico's other most-written character. So, they knew how to appeal to their audience! Fun fact, the person who wrote this asked me what my favorite tea was and how I would describe it… and that's how Chai entered this tale? I really don't know why my favorite tea had any bearing over Nico's gift, but, it did! So. There we go!

This is a pencil sketch of Faeowynn with Darius, a GAW-related critter. It's cute, I like it, but Darius definitely needs to at least cuss, heheh! Make him say "I'm the fucking star" or something like that. I kid, I kid. Very festive, well done.

UraniumEmpire's gift
Olney Ironworks

This is a great little piece about industrialism and capitalist greed. Not like we don't have a million of that on the site already, but… I like the angle here. I don't fully get the data expunged bits. I don't really know if all the variations on the cows are necessary, even if some are delightfully creepy. I like the containment procedures just keeping things as they are, and I like the comment about futility at the end. Pretty great, here. I imagine that if I knew anything about Olney Ironworks, I'd like this even more. I bet Uranium loves it.

Westrin's gift
The Squirrels in the Walls

This is a delightfully silly tale about some researchers arguing about how much they can afford to house 2,000,000 squirrels in this one site. Then, an out lands in their lap. It's simple, I'm definitely missing context (what does this have to do about being in the middle of an apocalypse?) such as reading the associated SCPs, but I like it regardless. Love the knocking on the walls and having squirrel sounds respond. Chitter, chitter, chitter.

YellisISlol's gift
Josie!

This is a perfect gift for someone who loves Josie the Half Cat, and also asked about hot chocolate being featured in their tale they got. It's simple, it's cute, it meets all the giftee's wishes, who could ask for more? Josie content, anomalous eggnog, cats batting at ornaments. Merry Christmas.

Yossipossi's gifts
Not Sure Yet

This is a story about some guys coming into contact with a Celtic god and living to tell the tale. I liked how obvious the guy's fake name was, and then that they brought it up instead of ignoring it, giving you this brief period of time where you're questioning whether the author thinks you're stupid or not, and then bringing it back around to clever when, later, the agents go "what a lazy way to hide your identity" (before the character is otherwise outed as a god). I liked it, props!

This is another tale Yossi got. It's definitely got some context I'm missing, since I've never really read any Undervegas stuff and — oh, whoops, spoilers? — that's what this tale ends with. "Welcome to Undervegas." I liked the dialogue, successfully makes me interested in Yossarian Leiner as a character, and both these tales make me more interested in Tactical Theology as a concept. After the 343 joke and the guy at the refreshments table consistently interrupting when Leiner asked who they were and how they knew all this stuff about Leiner made me half-expect the dude to be 343 himself, heheh.

Zyn's gift
We All Get Better

Awww. This is a really sweet tale in which the members of Kiryu labs unwittingly return something very important to someone back to them in their time of need. It's very heartwarming, and perfect for the season.
